standard.title: Locate, collect and record information
standard.description: locate, collect and record information and data from a range of sources, including annotated timelines and maps
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S02): Students located and evaluated sources and constructed annotated timelines and maps using cartographic conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate, collect and record information from discipline-appropriate sources using annotated timelines, maps, graphs and tables.

nodes.label: Discipline-appropriate sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify source types suited to different inquiry contexts (historical, geographical, civic) and explain why each is appropriate.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one appropriate source type for each of two different inquiry contexts and explain why each is suited.
nodes.typical_width: Identify sources suited to historical (paintings, maps, written accounts), geographical (thematic maps, satellite imagery, field data) and civic inquiry (newspaper articles, databases, interviews with local government); discuss why particular sources suit particular contexts.
wider: Evaluate the strengths and limitations of different source types for a specific inquiry question
Compare what information is available from digital vs non-digital sources for the same inquiry topic
nodes.hinge_reason: Discipline-appropriate source selection is the Year 4 research capability — without being able to match sources to inquiry contexts, the graphing and organisation tasks in Node 2 lack methodological grounding.

response_modes.reason: Source-context matching requires explicit reasoning: 'For a historical question I need... for a geographical question I need...' — scaffold with worked examples.

success_criteria: Identifies appropriate source types for at least two different inquiry contexts
Explains why each source type suits that context

nodes.label: Organising information in multiple formats
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use graphic organisers, timelines, maps, graphs and tables to display collected data and information.
nodes.minimum_width: Organise collected information in at least two different formats (e.g. a timeline and a table).
nodes.typical_width: Use food webs, consequence wheels, timelines of the First Fleet, maps of vegetation or peoples' movement, graphs of cultural groups in Australian society, and tables of data — selected appropriately for the type of information.
wider: Create a connected multi-format presentation where a map, timeline and table each present different aspects of the same inquiry
Evaluate which format best communicates specific types of information and argue for a choice

response_modes.reason: Multi-format organisation integrates research with data literacy — the matching of data type to display format is the integration task.

success_criteria: Organises information in at least two different formats
Format choice is appropriate for the type of information being displayed
